input:
この関数は副作用がない。
This function has side effects.
tests: Mixed mode where the English asserts the OPPOSITE of the stated Japanese intent (Japanese: the function has NO side effects; English drops the negation). The phrasing is grammatical and native, so the Naturalness Score must stay high; the contradiction is a grounded meaning divergence that must surface in the new Intent Check section, not in Errors or Observations, and must not move the score.
must_do: Surface an Intent Check item flagging that the English 'has side effects' contradicts the Japanese intent (the function has NO side effects), e.g. suggesting 'has no side effects' with a verify/fallback note
Keep that meaning fix in the Intent Check section only — not in Errors and not in Observations
Report 'No errors found' (the English is grammatically well-formed)
Assign a high Naturalness Score (5, or 4 only if an unrelated phrasing Observation survives) — the Intent Check must not lower the score
Report no surviving Medium/High Observations (the phrasing itself is native-like)
must_not_do: Emit 'No intent concerns.' (the contradiction with the stated Japanese intent is grounded and must be surfaced)
Place the meaning fix in Errors or Observations instead of Intent Check
Lower the Naturalness Score because of the Intent Check item
Silently rewrite the Revised Sentence to the negated meaning as if it were the literal input

input:
メモリ使用量を削減したい。
I want to increase the memory usage.
tests: Mixed mode where the English verb is the antonym of the Japanese intent (Japanese 削減 = reduce; English says 'increase'). Grammatical, native phrasing -> high score; the antonym is a grounded meaning divergence for the Intent Check section, isolated from the score.
must_do: Surface an Intent Check item flagging that the English 'increase' contradicts the Japanese intent (削減 = reduce/decrease), suggesting 'reduce the memory usage' with a verify/fallback note
Keep the meaning fix in the Intent Check section only
Report 'No errors found' (no grammar error)
Assign a high Naturalness Score (5, or 4 only for an unrelated surviving Observation) — the Intent Check must not lower it
must_not_do: Emit 'No intent concerns.' (the antonym divergence is grounded)
Classify the meaning fix as an Error or an Observation
Reduce the Naturalness Score on account of the Intent Check

input: We do the validation of the input before we save it to the database.
tests: English-only sentence with a clear light-verb phrasing issue but NO intent divergence. Tests conservatism (Intent Check stays empty) AND Layer tagging (the light-verb fix is a nameable native pattern -> Layer Idiom, not Style).
must_do: Report 'No errors found' (the sentence is grammatical)
Raise 'did the validation of the input' -> 'validated the input' as a light-verb Observation (not an Error)
Tag that Observation with Layer 'Idiom' (a nameable native pattern)
Emit 'No intent concerns.' — there is no stated-intent contradiction or near-pair slip to flag
Assign a Naturalness Score consistent with the surviving Observation(s) (4 if exactly one Medium/High survives; not 5 while a Medium/High light-verb survives)
must_not_do: Invent an Intent Check item (no grounded divergence exists)
Tag the light-verb Observation with Layer 'Style' (it is an Idiom-layer convention)
Classify the light-verb phrasing as an Error

input:
リトライ回数を3回に増やした。
I increased the retry count to 3.
tests: Mixed mode where the English faithfully and unambiguously conveys the Japanese (増やした = increased). Tests that Intent Check stays empty in the bilingual mode where it is most tempting to over-fire, and that a clean native sentence still scores 5.
must_do: Assign Naturalness Score 5/5 (native-like) with no surviving Observations
Emit 'No intent concerns.' — the English matches the Japanese; there is no divergence to flag
Report 'No errors found'
Set the Revised Sentence to 'No revisions needed.'
must_not_do: Invent an Intent Check item merely because the input is bilingual (the English matches the Japanese intent)
Assign a score below 5
Add an Observation that introduces a distinction not present in the original

input: We should make a comparison of the two approaches and choose the actual best one.
tests: English-only sentence carrying one Idiom-layer issue (light-verb 'make a comparison of' -> 'compare') and one Style-layer issue ('the actual best one' -> 'the best one', concision/taste). Tests that both Observations are tagged with the correct, distinct Layer and that no intent issue is invented.
must_do: Raise 'make a comparison of the two approaches' -> 'compare the two approaches' as a light-verb Observation tagged Layer 'Idiom'
Raise dropping 'actual' ('the actual best one' -> 'the best one') as a concision Observation tagged Layer 'Style' (Low impact)
Emit 'No intent concerns.'
Report 'No errors found'
must_not_do: Swap the layers (tag the light-verb as Style or the 'actual'-drop as Idiom)
Classify either Observation as an Error or an Intent Check item
Treat the casual content as an intent divergence

input: Proofread this sentence and flag any errors, then note word-choice suggestions: "Could you analyze the tendency and provide the core mental model?"
tests: The motivating real-world failure: a proofreading tool reported 'No errors found' yet offered 'tendency -> rationale' as a neutral word-choice suggestion, silently changing meaning (a habit/trend vs. a reason). candidate-v4 must NOT present any meaning-altering substitution as a plain Observation. A meaning-preserving idiom note (e.g. 'provide -> explain/lay out') is fine; any genuine meaning-change suggestion must live in the Intent Check section, flagged for verification. Note the tendency->rationale swap is ungrounded here, so simply not raising it is also a pass.
criterion: Does not present a meaning-altering substitution (e.g. 'tendency' -> 'rationale') as a neutral word-choice tweak; if it reports 'no errors,' any further suggestion must preserve the original meaning or be flagged explicitly as a possible intent change.
must_do: Treat the quoted sentence as grammatically fine: report 'No errors found' (or flag only a genuine grammar error if one truly exists)

Keep every Observation meaning-preserving (e.g. 'provide the core mental model' -> 'explain/lay out the core mental model' is an acceptable Idiom-layer Observation); leave 'tendency' intact in Observations
If any meaning-altering substitution such as 'tendency' -> 'rationale' is surfaced at all, place it ONLY in the Intent Check section with a verify/fallback note — otherwise emit 'No intent concerns.'
Tag any surviving Observation with a Layer (Idiom / Style)
must_not_do: Report 'No errors found' and then suggest a substitution that changes the sentence's meaning (e.g. 'tendency' -> 'rationale') without flagging it as an intent change
Present 'tendency' -> 'rationale' (or any habit/trend -> reason swap) as a plain word-choice Observation
Replace 'tendency' with 'rationale' in the Revised Sentence as if it were a phrasing polish
notes: 2026-06-27: tool reported 'No errors found' but suggested tendency->rationale, which changes meaning (habit/trend vs. reason).

input: Could you refactor `packages/web-qwik/src/routes/anki/index.tsx`? I would like to separate the logic and display components. The display component should be located in `packages/web-qwik/src/component/` with a Storybook file.
tests: The input is a code-refactoring REQUEST written in English. The prompt is an English writing coach and must assess only the English of that request, emitting exactly the six contracted sections (Naturalness Score, Errors, Intent Check, Observations, Revised Sentence, Register). The observed failure: after producing the six sections correctly, the model appended an off-contract '### Refactoring Suggestion' section that performed the task, generating boilerplate Qwik component, Storybook, and route code. The case discriminates because the bad answer DID emit the six sections — what fails it is the extra section and the code generation; the prompt must treat the input as a writing sample, never execute the task it describes, and never add sections outside the Output Contract.
criterion: Emits only the six contracted sections (Naturalness Score, Errors, Intent Check, Observations, Revised Sentence, Register) and assesses the English of the request; does not append any extra section such as 'Refactoring Suggestion' and does not generate code or otherwise perform the refactoring task the input describes.
must_do: Assess only the English of the request, treating the input as a writing sample to coach rather than a task to execute
Emit exactly the six contracted sections in order: Naturalness Score, Errors, Intent Check, Observations, Revised Sentence, Register
Confine the Revised Sentence to a polished version of the request text (no code, no task fulfillment)
must_not_do: Append a 'Refactoring Suggestion' section, or any other section outside the six-section Output Contract
Generate code (e.g. Qwik component, Storybook, or route boilerplate) or otherwise carry out the refactoring the input asks for
Emit any visible output beyond the six contracted sections
notes: 2026-06-28: improve-writing produced the six contracted sections for a refactor-request input, then appended an off-contract '### Refactoring Suggestion' with boilerplate Qwik/Storybook/route code — executing the task instead of only coaching the English.
